name: Summary list
summary: Use a summary list to present related key-and-value facts, optionally with contextual actions or a summary-card heading.
whenToUse: Use for facts that each have a clear key and at least one value.
Use summary cards for several records of the same type, such as people or appointments.
Add actions when users can change or remove the corresponding information.
whenNotToUse: Do not use for tabular comparisons; use a Table.
Do not use for an ordinary sequence or task list.
Do not force content without a meaningful key-value relationship into a description list.

anatomy.name: Description list
anatomy.description: A govuk-summary-list dl contains repeated row wrappers.

anatomy.name: Key and value
anatomy.description: Each row contains a dt key and dd value.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.description: An optional dd contains links with visually hidden row context.

anatomy.name: Card heading
anatomy.description: A summary card can group a list with a heading and whole-card actions.

variants.name: Without borders
variants.use: A short simple list where row borders add unnecessary visual weight.

variants.name: Summary card
variants.use: One of several comparable records requiring its own heading or actions.

behaviour: No GOV.UK JavaScript module is required and action links use ordinary href navigation.
Keep rows in a meaningful order and retain the semantic dl, dt and dd elements.
After a change action, return users to the correct review context where possible.
accessibility: Add visually hidden key context to repeated action labels, for example “Change name”.
Set the card heading level to fit the page hierarchy.
Do not create empty keys or values merely to preserve a visual grid.
content: Keep keys concise and use the same terms as the questions that collected the data.
Format values for reading rather than exposing raw storage values.
Use consistent action verbs such as “Change” and “Remove”.
